title: LayerNorm
summary: Layer normalization independently normalizes the final four-feature dimension of two rows, then applies learned elementwise scale and bias.
example:
import torch
from torch import nn

x = torch.tensor([[1, 2, 3, 4], [2, 0, 2, 0]], device="cuda")
norm = nn.LayerNorm(4, eps=1e-5, elementwise_affine=True).cuda()
with torch.no_grad():
    norm.weight.copy_(torch.tensor([1, 1.5, 0.5, 2], device="cuda"))
    norm.bias.copy_(torch.tensor([0, 1, 0, -1], device="cuda"))
y = norm(x)
limitations: Fixed fixture normalizes the last dimension of size 4 for two rows, uses population variance and ε=1e-5.
This example omits mixed precision, alternate normalized shapes, affine=False, backward pass, and backend fusion.

tensors.name: input
tensors.description: Two rows normalized independently across four features.

tensors.name: normalized
tensors.description: Centered and variance-scaled values before affine parameters.

tensors.name: output
tensors.description: Normalized values after per-feature scale and shift.

stages.title: Per-row mean and variance
stages.summary: One output thread recomputes the mean and population variance over its row’s four features.
stages.insight: Each row is a separate normalization group; variance divides by four, not three.

stages.title: Normalize and apply affine parameters
stages.summary: Center by the row mean, divide by the stabilized standard deviation, then multiply gamma and add beta.
stages.insight: The fixture retains learned affine scale and shift instead of stopping at normalized values.
